title: Reading a conversation before you resume it

steps.path: The sessions arrow at the top of the window, then Resume
steps.headline: Show the conversation you have picked, on the right of the Resume window.
steps.changed: Clicking a conversation in the list fills the right side with what was actually said in it, so you can read the end of it before you decide to go back in.
steps.measured: The window goes from 450 px wide to 1000 px
steps.notice: This is running in the real app, but against made-up conversations — the words inside the transcript are invented. The layout, spacing and controls are the real ones.
steps.risk: The window is twice as wide. Below 640 px — a phone, or the remote browser on a small screen — it stays exactly as it is today, list only, because a transcript and a list cannot share that width.

steps.headline: Where should Model, Launch in New Window and the Resume button live?
steps.notice: The whole window each time. Watch the right half for the controls, and the list on the left for whether the card you clicked opens up.
steps.risk: Today those controls open up inside the card you clicked, and every card below it slides down the list. Two of these three stop that from happening.

variants.label: Leave them in the list
variants.summary: The right side is only the conversation. The card you clicked still opens up in the list with the controls in it, exactly as it does now.
variants.risk: Two things move when you click a row: the list grows a card and the right side fills. The Resume button ends up on the opposite side of the window from what you are reading.

variants.label: Under the conversation
variants.summary: The controls sit beneath the transcript, on the right. The cards in the list never open up again, so the list stops jumping around.
variants.risk: Model and both switches are on screen the whole time, even while you are only reading.

variants.label: Behind a Resume button
variants.summary: The right side is only the conversation, with a Resume button in the corner. Pressing it drops the same controls in above the transcript. This is how the session drawer already behaves.
variants.risk: Resuming takes two presses instead of one.

steps.path: The right half, before you have clicked anything
steps.headline: What should the right half show in the moment before you have picked a conversation?
steps.notice: This is the state the window opens in, every single time.

options.label: One line of text
pros: Nothing is read off disk that you did not ask for.
The window opens the same way every time.
cons: Half the window is empty at the moment you open it.
You have to click once before you learn anything you did not already know.

options.label: Open the most recent one
pros: The window is useful the second it appears.
Getting back to what you were last working on takes no clicks at all.
cons: A conversation is read every time you open the window, whether you wanted it or not.
The top row is always highlighted, which can read as 'already chosen'.
